notes.text: Ministered — That is, performed his ministration carefully and faithfully. Before the Lord - In God's tabernacle. Ephod - A garment used in God's service, and allowed not only to the inferior priests and Levites but also to eminent persons of the people, and therefore to Samuel, who, though no Levite, was a Nazarite, from his birth.

glossa.text: *A tunic.* The tunic which Anna, that is grace, made and delivered to the boy; it is the beginning doctrine by which the faithful receive the first rudiments, whence: *I gave you milk to drink, not meat ((I Cor. III))*. But the linen ephod signifies chastity and continence together with good works. For he who desires to minister to the Lord must needs live chastely and continently, and exercise himself in good works.

notes.text: Heavens of heavens — Ye highest heavens, the place of God's throne. Waters - Ye clouds which are above a part of the heavens.
Established — He hath made them constant and incorruptible, not changeable, as the things of the lower world. A decree - Concerning their continuance.
Dragons — Either serpents, which hide in the deep caverns of the earth; or whales, and other sea-monsters, which dwell in the depths of the sea.

Fire — Lightnings and other fireworks of the air. Vapor - Or, fumes: hot exhalations. Fulfilling his word - Executing his commands, either for the comfort or punishment of the inhabitants of the earth.
Above — Above all the glories which are in earth and in heaven.

The horn — In scripture commonly denotes strength, victory, glory, and felicity. An exhortation to praise God for his love to his people, ver. 1-5. And for enabling them to overcome their enemies, ver. 6- 9.

glossa.text: *Praise ye the Lord from the heavens.* ((CASS.)) By the mention of a few he exhorts the whole creation to praise God. There are certain things which have a spirit of praising God in that affection wherewith God pleases them: certain have no understanding, but because they themselves are good in their own order, and are referred to the beauty of the whole, they praise not of themselves, but by them God is praised through those that consider them: and so after a sort they praise, because from them the praise of God is born in us, whereto the prophet here admonishes us.

*For he spoke, and they were made.* ((CASS.)) This against those who say that the world is coeternal with God; there follows: *He commanded.* By his word, and they were created. First he said, *made,* afterward *created.* For make we also can, but not create. He therefore alone creates, which is proper to the Godhead. Praise from his works

*He hath established.* From his power he is almighty, whose works are not changed.

*Unto the age, and unto the age of the age.* ((CAS.)) And though the heaven be new, yet they are said to be well established by God, which are made new through Christ and remain bettered. And here is praise from his power.

*Praise ye the Lady *Dominam*; read *Dominum*, "the Lord".* The second part, where, the heavenly things being enumerated, he descends to earthly things. Turning therefore to them, as exhorting us that by the consideration of them we may praise God, which things considered lay open the praise of God, he says: O ye that are of the earth. *All ye deeps.* *ubyssi* ((AUG.)) The depth of the waters, etc., *as far as* these therefore, that is, he exhorts us to praise by the consideration of them.

*Which do his word.* This therefore because it seemed to certain men that God ruled the higher things, but despised these lower ones, and that they were ruled by chance; but these also God does, and in these least things he is praised, and alleluia is sung.

*Confession.* ((CAS.)) Above he spoke first of heaven, afterward of earth; here of all together. And he takes by heaven all higher things, and by earth all lower things. ((AUG.)) *His confession above heaven and earth.* All things confess him in themselves or in others; the beauty of all things is the voice of them that confess, in those who consider them, that is, let those who consider praise him, both from earthly and from heavenly things, than which there is nothing better.
*He hath exalted the horn of his people.* ((ID.)) Behold what Aggeus and Zacharias prophesied. Now the horn of his people is lowly in tribulations, but when the Lord shall come, it shall be exalted.

notes.text: All who are thus renewed are elected of God, holy, and therefore the more beloved of him. Holiness is the consequence of their election, and God's superior love, of their holiness.
Forbearing one another — If anything is now wrong. And forgiving one another - What is past.
The love of God contains the whole of Christian perfection, and connects all the parts of it together.
And then the peace of God shall rule in your hearts — Shall sway every temper, affection, thought, as the reward (so the Greek word implies) of your preceding love and obedience.

Let the word of Christ — So the apostle calls the whole scripture, and thereby asserts the divinity of his Master. Dwell - Not make a short stay, or an occasional visit, but take up its stated residence. Richly - In the largest measure, and with the greatest efficacy; so as to fill and govern the whole soul.
In the name — In the power and Spirit of the Lord Jesus. Giving thanks unto God - The Holy Ghost. And the Father through him - Christ.

glossa.text: *Charity.* For it is itself the more eminent way, which is above knowledge and all precepts. This is the seamless garment of the Lord, woven from above. Seamless, lest at any time it be unsewn, which reaches to one, because charity gathers all into one.
*Peace.* This is necessary to the unity of the body, which it has itself made. *The peace of God.* There can be called a peace which has not charity; but charity always has peace with itself.
*Teaching and admonishing.* He says this, that there may be teaching for those who know not, and admonition for those who know.

*All whatsoever.* Because above he commanded God to be praised in the heart, now he exhorts that the name of God be praised and exalted both in words and in deeds: so that our words and works may thus lack reproof, that the Lord may be magnified, by whose teaching the disciples are unblameable. *All things.* Not only what you do in word or in deed, but all things, even thoughts, and if there be any others. Or, whatever you do, do the whole, that is, the perfect, by attributing it to God, and this is, doing in the name. *Giving thanks.* Then do we truly give thanks to God through Christ, if we keep the measure of his precepts.

notes.text: The child Jesus — St. Luke describes in order Jesus the fruit of the womb, chap. i, 42; an infant, chap. ii, 12; a little child, ver. 40; a child here, and afterward a man. So our Lord passed through and sanctified every stage of human life. Old age only did not become him.
Supposing him to have been in the company — As the men and women usually travelled in distinct companies.

After three days — The first day was spent in their journey, the second, in their return to Jerusalem: and the third, in searching for him there: they found him in the temple - In an apartment of it: sitting in the midst of the doctors - Not one word is said of his disputing with them, but only of his asking and answering questions, which was a very usual thing in these assemblies, and indeed the very end of them. And if he was, with others, at the feet of these teachers (where learners generally sat) he might be said to be in the midst of them, as they sat on benches of a semicircular form, raised above their hearers and disciples.
Why sought ye me? — He does not blame them for losing, but for thinking it needful to seek him: and intimates, that he could not be lost, nor found any where, but doing the will of a higher parent.
It is observable that Joseph is not mentioned after this time; whence it is probable, he did not live long after.

Jesus increased in wisdom — As to his human nature, and in favour with God - In proportion to that increase. It plainly follows, that though a man were pure, even as Christ was pure, still he would have room to increase in holiness, and in consequence thereof to increase in the favour, as well as in the love of God.

glossa.text: *And his parents went,* etc. ((ID.)) Deservedly Luke is compared, among the four living creatures, to the calf, etc., *as far as* at the end of his Gospel he concludes with the disciples of the Lord praising in the temple.
*And not finding him. ((ID.))* If it is asked how he could be left behind by his parents through forgetfulness, etc., *as far as* returned with the other parent.

*In the midst. ((ID.))* As a fountain, he sits in the midst of the doctors; but as a pattern of humility, he asks and hears before he instructs, lest little ones should blush to be taught by their elders, lest one who is weak should dare to teach.

*How is it that you sought me? ((ID.))* He does not find fault with their seeking him as a son, but he suggests who is his true Father, and compels them to lift the eyes of the mind to what is rather owed to him whose eternal Son he is. For because he is God and man, now he sets forth the lofty things of the Godhead, now the weak things of the humanity. As the Son of God he stays in the temple; as the Son of man he goes back with his parents whither they bid.

*And his mother kept all these words in her heart.* All the things which she knew to have been done concerning the Lord or by the Lord, whether those she understood or those she could not yet understand, she laid up all in her memory, so that, when the time should come for his incarnation to be preached or written, she might be able sufficiently to set forth to those who asked all things just as they had been done. So let us, by frequent meditation on the deeds and words of the Lord, drive off importunate thoughts and labour to instruct others.
*He advanced in wisdom. ((BEDA.))* As it belongs to the flesh to advance in age, etc., *as far as* both alike might be saved.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples:
echoes.note: "As God's chosen ones, holy and beloved" transfers to the church Israel's defining triad: chosen, a holy people, beloved by the LORD's set love. High coherence and recurrence; the election language (eklektoi, hagioi, egapemenoi) maps directly onto Deuteronomy's covenant self-description of Israel.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
echoes.note: "Compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance" reproduces the cluster of the divine attributes proclaimed at Sinai (compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love). High recurrence: this is the OT's signature self-revelation of God's character, and believers are to put it on in imitation. Coherence with the forgiving-as-the-Lord-forgave clause is exact.

echoes.text: Yahweh is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.
echoes.note: "The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in mercy" is the psalmist's reuse of Exod 34:6 and supplies the same attribute-list the believer dons. Strong recurrence of the formula; the surrounding theme of God's forgiveness (Ps 103:12) coheres with "even as Christ forgave you" in v.13.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: "Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection" rests on the love command of the Holiness Code, the OT verse Paul treats as summing up neighbor-ethics. High coherence: love crowning and binding the virtue list functions as the fulfillment of Lev 19:18; strong recurrence in Pauline paraenesis.

echoes.text: The animals of the field shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen, the people which I formed for myself, that they might declare my praise.
echoes.note: "My chosen people... which I formed for myself" stands behind "God's chosen ones," the elect people gathered to declare God's praise. Supports the high-confidence election cluster; medium because Deut 7 is the more controlling source, with Isaiah reinforcing the chosen-and-beloved motif.

echoes.text: Tear your heart, and not your garments, and turn to Yahweh, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
echoes.note: The gracious-and-compassionate, slow-to-anger formula also appears in Joel and could feed the attribute cluster of v.12. Low/secondary; Exod 34:6 and Ps 103:8 are the primary witnesses, with Joel one of several prophetic reuses of the same liturgical formula.

echoes.text: Give thanks to Yahweh with the lyre. Sing praises to him with the harp of ten strings. Sing to him a new song. Play skillfully with a shout of joy!
echoes.note: "Psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace" echoes the psalter's call to sing a new song with skill and praise. Medium volume; "psalms" is itself the genre word, and the threefold list of sung praise coheres with Israel's temple-song tradition the term presupposes.

echoes.text: Then on that day David first ordained to give thanks to Yahweh, by the hand of Asaph and his brothers. Oh give thanks to Yahweh. Call on his name. Make his doings known among the peoples. Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works. Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice. Seek Yahweh and his strength. Seek his face forever more. Remember his marvelous works that he has done, his wonders, and the […]
echoes.note: The injunction to teach and admonish with psalms and thanksgiving recalls David's appointment of song and thanks before the ark. Faint; contact is the institution of communal praise/thanksgiving ("be thankful," v.15) rather than any quoted line, so volume is low.

echoes.text: Moreover, David and the captains of the army set apart for the service certain of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with stringed instruments, and with cymbals: and the number of those who did the work according to their service was: of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, and Joseph, and Nethaniah, and Asharelah, the sons of Asaph, under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied after the order of the king. Of Jeduthun; the […]
echoes.note: "Spiritual songs" and the temple-singer guilds set apart to prophesy with music stand behind the Christian assembly's sung instruction. Low/contested; the link is the institutional background of inspired temple song, not verbal citation.

echoes.text: These words, which I command you this day, shall be on your heart; and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
echoes.note: "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly... teaching and admonishing" coheres with the Shema's command to let God's words remain in the heart and to teach them diligently. Faint; the indwelling-and-teaching-the-word motif is suggestive but generic to Deuteronomic catechesis.

echoes.text: but his delight is in Yahweh’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.
echoes.note: The word dwelling in believers richly resonates with the blessed one whose delight is in the law, meditating on it day and night. Low volume and contested; thematic overlap (the indwelling, treasured word) without lexical contact.

echoes.text: Give thanks to Yahweh! Call on his name! Make his doings known among the peoples.
echoes.note: "Do all in the name of the Lord... giving thanks" echoes the psalmist's "give thanks to the LORD, call upon his name." Faint; the thanks-and-the-name pairing is a stock liturgical formula recurring across the psalter, so no single verse controls.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh, and also with men.
echoes.note: The closing 'Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men' restates Samuel's growth 'in favor with the LORD and with men,' an inclusio with v. 40. Strong verbal parallel and double recurrence make this the chapter's clearest growth-formula allusion.

echoes.text: You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it you came out of Egypt), and no one shall appear before me empty.
echoes.note: The family's annual Passover pilgrimage to Jerusalem enacts the Torah requirement that all appear before the LORD at the appointed feasts, the first being Unleavened Bread/Passover. The pilgrimage-feast obligation gives the scene its legal frame and coherence with Luke's law-observant family.

echoes.text: Observe the month of Abib, and keep the Passover to Yahweh your God; for in the month of Abib Yahweh your God brought you out of Egypt by night. You shall sacrifice the Passover to Yahweh your God, of the flock and the herd, in the place which Yahweh shall choose, to cause his name to dwell there. You shall eat no leavened bread with it. You shall eat unleavened bread with it seven days, even the bread of affliction; for you came out of the land of Egypt […]
echoes.note: Going up 'every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover' follows the Deuteronomic centralization of Passover at the place the LORD chooses, i.e., Jerusalem. Availability is direct and coherence exact for the pilgrimage detail in vv. 41-42.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: Jesus is found in the temple declaring he 'must be in my Father's house,' the Lord present in his own temple as Malachi foretold and as Simeon's temple-encounter anticipated. The temple-claim coheres with the Father-Son relation Luke develops and recurs across the chapter's temple scenes.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying, “This month shall be to you the beginning of months. It shall be the first month of the year to you. Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth day of this month, they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses, a lamb for a household; and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one […]
echoes.note: The explicit Passover setting frames Jesus' first recorded words against the founding redemption feast, a figural touch given Luke's later Passion-Passover. The connection is contextual rather than verbal here, so a faint echo at this point in the narrative.

echoes.text: “Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways. Hear instruction, and be wise. Don’t refuse it. Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts. For whoever finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from Yahweh.
echoes.note: The boy 'filled with wisdom,' astonishing the teachers and increasing 'in wisdom,' is colored by Wisdom's call to the children who keep her ways and find favor from the LORD. The wisdom-and-favor coherence is real but the sapiential coloring is diffuse, so a faint echo.

echoes.text: Now I was a child of parts, and a good soul fell to my lot; Nay rather, being good, I came into a body undefiled. But perceiving that I could not otherwise possess wisdom except God gave her me (Yes and to know by whom the grace is given, this too came of understanding), I pleaded with the Lord and implored him, and with my whole heart I said,
echoes.note: The precociously wise child amazing his elders resembles the ideal in Wisdom where the speaker, 'a child of good parts,' receives wisdom as a gift sought in the sanctuary. The early-wisdom motif is coherent within Second-Temple thought, though not a verbal source.

echoes.text: Stand you in the multitude of the elders; And whoso is wise, cleave you to him. Be willing to listen to every godly discourse; And don’t let the proverbs of understanding escape you. If you see a man of understanding, get you betimes to him, And let your foot wear out the steps of his doors. Let your mind dwell upon the ordinances of the Lord, And meditate continually in his commandments: He will establish your heart, And your desire of wisdom will be […]
echoes.note: Jesus 'sitting in the midst of the teachers, both listening and asking questions' embodies Ben Sira's counsel to stand in the assembly of elders, attach oneself to the wise, and meditate on the law. The disciple-among-the-sages image coheres, but the link is thematic and faint.

echoes.text: One thing I have asked of Yahweh, that I will seek after, that I may dwell in Yahweh’s house all the days of my life, to see Yahweh’s beauty, and to inquire in his temple.
echoes.note: Jesus' devotion to being 'in my Father's house' resonates with the psalmist's one desire 'to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life.' The longing-for-God's-house theme is coherent but generic, hence a faint supporting echo.

echoes.text: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
echoes.note: 'After three days they found him' has occasionally been read against Hosea's 'on the third day he will raise us up,' a figural foreshadowing of the resurrection found-on-the-third-day. The three-days detail offers verbal contact, but the application is debated, so a contested faint echo.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights.
Let us clothe ourselves with love.
The child grew, and the favor of God was upon him.
Let us clothe ourselves with love.
Whatever you do, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The angels have gone; the shepherds have gone home. The work of an ordinary life begins.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
A boy grows up in Nazareth, year by quiet year, in wisdom and in grace.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
So we put on, like clothing, compassion and kindness and patience.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
And over it all we put on love, which binds everything together.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised forever!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The shepherds gone home, an ordinary life begins.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
A child grows in wisdom and in grace.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised.
Clothe yourselves with love, and do all in his name.
Praise the Lord; let his name be praised. Amen.
